title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. Generated video was used to put statements into a candidate's mouth that she never made, and the output was published to a social platform as if it were her speech. The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation: the videos were posted to X by the opposing campaign, which is where the false statements reached an audience.

Catching it required knowing what the real person actually said. The statements attributed to Cooke were fabricated, and the only reliable check was against her actual record, which her attorneys supplied when they said she never made them. No platform-side or automated check is described in the reporting as having flagged the videos before or after posting.

What is not established is whether the videos were intended as satire, whether any defamation claim will be filed, and whether the statements caused measurable harm. A cease-and-desist letter is a demand, not a ruling, and the campaign's dismissal of it is a response, not a defence.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says Cooke never made those statements and warns Van Orden could face defamation claims under state law.

Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum. Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring his social media accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden responded this week with another AI-generated video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!" Cooke previously lost to Van Orden in 2024 by about 3 percentage points.
